classification.difficultyReason: Direct application of acute reference angles and ASTC, with diagrams supplied for the first three parts.

content.prompt: Rewrite these trigonometric ratios in terms of their acute reference angles.

spec.description: Circle and four-ended axes with a terminal radius at 130 degrees. Distinct blue given-angle and red acute reference-angle sectors.
spec.mathematics: The terminal radius lies in quadrant II; A is the angle between the negative horizontal axis and the terminal radius.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram content is supplied and remains visible in the question edition.

answer.worked:
$A=180^{\circ}-130^{\circ}=50^{\circ}$. Tangent is negative in quadrant II.
$$\tan130^{\circ}=-\tan50^{\circ}$$

spec.description: Circle and four-ended axes with a terminal radius at 310 degrees. The blue sweep is reflex; the red reference sector is the remaining acute angle.
spec.mathematics: The terminal radius lies in quadrant IV; A is between the positive horizontal axis and terminal radius.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram content is supplied and remains visible in the question edition.

answer.worked:
$A=360^{\circ}-310^{\circ}=50^{\circ}$. Cosine is positive in quadrant IV.
$$\cos310^{\circ}=\cos50^{\circ}$$

spec.description: Circle and four-ended axes with a terminal radius at 220 degrees. Blue reflex sweep and separate red acute reference sector.

spec.answerVisibility: All diagram content is supplied and remains visible in the question edition.
